name: ab_layout
description: Map an unencrypted Android adb backup (.ab) onto the layout ALEAPP reads, and call the result what it is: a derivative of an adb backup, never a file-system acquisition. The file is the header ANDROID BACKUP, a format version, a compression flag and an encryption scheme, then a tar (deflated with zlib when the flag says so) whose members the backup agent named apps/<package>/_manifest and apps/<package>/<domain>/<path>, and shared/<n>/<path> for shared storage. The tool streams the tar once and, for copy_content, writes under $OUT/ab_layout/derivative: data/data/<package>/... (and data/user_de/0/<package>/... for the device-protected tokens), ab_layout_meta/<package>/_manifest (the package's manifest record, kept apart from the data tree) and DERIVATIVE.json (the banner: kind 'derivative of an adb backup', and that it is not a file-system acquisition); the answer says 'derivative of an adb backup' too. MAPPING TABLE (the FullBackup domain token of a member -> where its path goes): `r` -> data/data/<package> (the package's root), `f` -> data/data/<package>/files, `db` -> data/data/<package>/databases, `sp` -> data/data/<package>/shared_prefs, `nb` -> data/data/<package>/no_backup, `c` -> data/data/<package>/cache, `d_r` -> data/user_de/0/<package>, `d_f` -> data/user_de/0/<package>/files, `d_db` -> data/user_de/0/<package>/databases, `d_sp` -> data/user_de/0/<package>/shared_prefs, `d_nb` -> data/user_de/0/<package>/no_backup, `d_c` -> data/user_de/0/<package>/cache; `a` (the APK), `obb` and `ef` (external storage files) and everything under shared/ are listed and not extracted; any other token is an unknown domain, listed and not extracted, and the answer is partial. BASIS OF THE TABLE: the tokens and their meaning are those of FullBackup's tree-token constants in the Android platform source (apk a, obb, root r, files f, no_backup nb, databases db, shared_prefs sp, cache c, managed external ef, and the device-protected forms with the d_ prefix), as the author recalls them; the table has not been checked against the AOSP source for the Android versions in play (the source was not available when this was written), so a token the tool lists as unknown, or a mapping that a case disproves, is for the examiner to settle, and the table is the first thing to check. Which of these paths ALEAPP reads is likewise not verified here. The SQLite companions (-wal, -shm, -journal) are members like any other and are laid out beside their database (a companion with no base file in the same directory is counted). Bounds: header versions 1 to 5 are read (any other is unsupported and only the header is reported; the answer is failed), the payload is decompressed in pieces under max_decompressed_bytes (default 16 GiB, at most 1 TiB; a stream that expands past it stops the walk and the answer is partial), at most max_members members (default 200,000, at most 1,000,000) and max_bytes extracted in all (default 4 GiB; a member that would pass it is not started), the clock (max_seconds), an extended header over 1 MiB (the walk stops), at most 64 components and 4096 bytes in a name, and at most 2,000,000 names in the layout. The end of the stream is verified and anything else is partial: the zlib stream's end marker (reached, truncated, damaged, or not reached at the budget), the tar's two end blocks (a lone zero block with a header after it is read past and counted, a missing end is said, a header whose checksum does not hold ends the walk), zero padding after the end blocks (not data) and any other data after them, and bytes after the end of the zlib stream (counted, not read). A member name is hostile text: a name with '..' or '.' or an empty component, an absolute path, a NUL, a component over 255 bytes, a package that is not an Android package name, is rejected and listed with its reason and never written (a name that is only odd, such as ..config or ..., is a file name); two members on one name (a duplicate, names that differ only in case or in Unicode form, a file and a directory) each get their own name and say so in name_collision and in the answer's collisions; links, hard links, device nodes, FIFOs, directories and sparse members are listed and never created, followed or extracted. Every member read is a line of a result file the answer names, whole (the inline entries are a prefix and entry_count is the lines the file holds): the member name as spelled and its exact bytes in base64 (member_b64; null for a withheld name), its offset in the decompressed payload, size, type, mode, the raw time, package, domain, the state, the name in the layout and the SHA-256 of what was written. Files are written to a hidden temporary beside their name (registered for removal before it is made) and given their name by a hard link, so a stop leaves no half file under a final name; a second run in the same $OUT names identical files again and never replaces one (a changed member takes -2, and the answer says so). status is complete only when the payload was read to the end of its stream, the tar's end blocks were found with nothing after them, and every member that is laid out by design was extracted (in a plan: planned); otherwise partial with a status_basis that names why. Members the tool never extracts by design (directories, a, obb, ef, shared/, links, devices, FIFOs, packages left out by the packages filter) are listed with their state and do not make the answer partial; unknown domains, rejected names, names outside apps/ and shared/, sparse members, members left out by max_bytes, the clock or a refused write do. A write the file system refused is write_failed on that member (a full disk or a size limit also stops further extraction) and is not a fact about the backup. A write the file system refuses to the result file itself ends the run as failed, not as a row. NOT done: no decryption and no password is read or accepted (an AES-256 payload is refused after its header, which is the only part read); the derivative is not the phone; file times, owners and modes are not set on the copies; no SQLite database is opened or checked. SENSITIVE: copy_content writes the app data the backup holds, which can be secret. It is false by default (a plan: the whole inventory and mapping, nothing extracted) and is a secret_output mode of the manifest: accepted only in a job run as secret output (SECRET_OUTPUT=1) and otherwise refused as JSON before anything is made. A member name or package shaped like a recovery password (42 or more decimal digits with at most three characters that are neither a letter nor a digit between two digits, after NFKC folding, a key split across components included) is withheld from every channel: the answer, the result file and the names under the derivative carry the placeholder withheld-component, and the real member name is written only to a 0600 values file, ab-layout-values.jsonl (or -2, -3 ... beside an earlier one), created exclusively before anything is read, in a copy_content job. The packages filter is matched against package names as they are printed. Each row carries parser ab_layout/1. The answer is strict JSON.

path.description: The Android backup (.ab) file: a regular file, opened without waiting and without following a link

copy_content.description: Extract the members into the derivative (default false: a plan that writes only the result file). Accepted only in a job run as secret output (SECRET_OUTPUT=1); refused as JSON otherwise, before anything is made. Writes the 0600 values file for withheld names

packages.description: Only these Android package names (as the answer prints them); the other packages' members are listed as not_selected. At most 1000

max_members.description: Members read (default 200000, at most 1000000); the walk stops there and the answer says partial

max_bytes.description: Bytes extracted in all (default 4 GiB); a member that would pass it is not started and is listed as not_extracted_max_bytes

max_decompressed_bytes.description: The decompression budget (default 16 GiB, at most 1 TiB): a payload that expands past it stops the walk and the answer is partial

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock (default 240, at most 255): the walk ends at 93 % of it; the answer says partial and where it stopped

limit.description: Members, packages and collisions in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names
